title: docs: define lean MVP and no-argument TUI plan
body:
## Problem
The family has a strong canonical BF3 specification but no single, durable implementation plan for the lean first release and the requested no-argument TUI. Coordination notes alone do not define the executable order, state contract, recovery behavior, or release gate.

## Change
- add `docs/assurance/mvp-tui-delivery-plan.md`
- index the plan from `docs/README.md`
- define the one-owner/one-provider G1 scope, no-argument TUI journey, shared TUI/browser command contract, durable controller slices, fake-first fault matrix, Codex qualification, verification and draft-PR recovery rules
- preserve G2/G3 capabilities in the canonical backlog instead of pulling them into the MVP
- bind the plan to BF3 packages, performance targets, CI lanes, and the integrated interruption/recovery acceptance gate

## Validation
- `just docs` (passes; release truth remains intentionally BLOCKED by existing release policy)
- `git diff --check`
- branch created from current `origin/main`

This is documentation only. It does not add provider keys, grants, live execution, or operator decisions.

title: Make the scheduled lanes able to run at all
body:
**All four scheduled workflows had never executed once.** Their crons fire on Mondays, the repositories were created on a Wednesday, and `workflow_dispatch` was enabled the whole time — so 26 of 53 job definitions had never been observed. I dispatched three of them. Eleven jobs failed. Four of the five hub failures are fixed here.

## Windows could not check the repository out

Not the lane — the checkout.

```
error: invalid path 'fixtures/hostile/cases/nul.json'
##[error]The process 'git.exe' failed with exit code 128
```

`nul` is a reserved device name on Windows. Git cannot create that file, so **every Windows claim this repository has ever made is about a checkout that never happened.** Renamed to `nul-character.json`, which is what the fixture was always about — a NUL character inside JSON, not a filename. Same bytes, same `CONTROL_CHARACTER_FORBIDDEN` reason code; generator and consumer both updated.

## macOS could not install Python

```
##[error]The version '3.12.12' with architecture 'arm64' was not found for macOS 15.7.9
```

The exact patch was never load-bearing: `ops/ci/rust-toolchain-boundary.sh` accepts any `^Python 3\.12\.[0-9]+$` and then verifies the resolved binary by digest. The pin is now the **3.12 series**, in the workflow and in the guard that asserts it — which still stops a silent jump to 3.13, the thing that guard is actually for.

## Coverage never had a scanner

The coverage filter is the whole workspace, wider than the fast lane's partition, so it reaches `publication::scan::tests::actual_pinned_scanner_detects_binary_and_chunk_boundary_canaries`. That test **admits the pinned scanner rather than skipping**, so it panicked at `src/publication/scan_tests.rs:130`. The `fast` job already installs gitleaks for exactly this reason; now the coverage job does too.

## The links lane had never installed its own tool

```
##[error]install-action: install-action does not support lychee@0.24.0
```

`taiki-e/install-action` does not carry lychee at the pinned revision — it never has. `ops/ci/install-lychee.sh` replaces it in the same shape as `ops/ci/install-gitleaks.sh`: one named asset over TLS, checked against the digest upstream publishes beside it, refuse rather than continue.

Verified locally against the real documentation tree: **890 links, 889 OK, 0 errors.**

## The audit job is deliberately left failing

**Exit 78 is not neutral in GitHub Actions.** It never was — 78 was the neutral code for the old Apps check API and has never meant anything to a workflow step. Every "typed neutral refusal" written on that pattern is a red job wearing a polite message, in all four repositories.

It cannot be repaired in the workflow, because `ops/ci/artifact-check.sh` requires an observation whose `tool_versions` names `jankurai`, and there is no version to record when the tool is absent. That is a contract four repositories share, so it is not mine to decide alone. `~/.bullet-orch-durable/CI-PORTABILITY-FINDINGS-20260910.md` sets out three options and my preference.

## Also

Six of the eight publication workflow digest pins are re-admitted from the published mains, clearing `PUBLICATION_CI_WORKFLOW_DIGEST_DRIFT`. Topology unchanged; only bytes moved.

Proved on the development host before pushing: the full `lint` lane green, the workflow policy green with the new guard text, and the renamed fixture green through both `bullet-contract check` and the `canonical_hostile` suite.

title: Render the repair metadata CoordError has always carried, and give the CLI one colour rule
body:
The best error UX in the family was already built. It was just never printed.

Every `CoordError` carries four facts beyond its code and reason — the purpose of the boundary that refused, at least two concrete fixes, a narrow next step, and a repository-relative docs anchor. `repair_metadata` fills all four for every code, every anchor resolves in `docs/errors.md`, and a test already asserted there are never fewer than two fixes. The only consumers were four assertions in the test suite, because `Display` writes `{code}: {reason}` and nothing read the rest.

## Before

```
bullet-family: UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA: family.lock schema 2 is not installable; retain it for diagnosis, regenerate schema 3 from authenticated signed tags, and replace it atomically
```

## After

```
bullet-family: UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA
  family.lock schema 2 is not installable; retain it for diagnosis, regenerate schema 3 from authenticated signed tags, and replace it atomically

  protecting    reject a schema outside the admitted version set
  try           - follow the explicit export or removal procedure
                - use the binary and lock version that own the subject
  next          follow the schema-removal or setup-recovery runbook
  docs          docs/errors.md#unsupported-or-corrupt-state
```

## What is deliberately not changed

`Display` is untouched and stays `{code}: {reason}`. It is the machine contract, and a lot of tooling greps stderr for that shape. The rendered form still leads with the code on line one so those greps keep working on it too.

**The reason text is never hard-wrapped.** Wrapping it broke `release_profiles::ordinary_release_requires_an_explicit_profile`, which greps for a phrase that a newline had landed inside. That failure was the useful kind — it identifies exactly which text other people depend on. A terminal soft-wraps a long line for free, so only the metadata block, which nothing greps because until now it was never printed, is laid out to a width.

## One colour rule, no new dependency

`src/diagnostic.rs` decides colour once, from values passed in rather than looked up, so the rule is a pure function with tests:

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `NO_COLOR` present and non-empty | never paint |
| `CLICOLOR_FORCE` non-empty and not `0` | paint even a pipe |
| `TERM` `dumb` or absent | never paint, even when forced |
| otherwise | the depth the terminal advertises |

Three depth tiers — basic, 256, truecolor — because a palette that emits truecolor unconditionally is a bet, not a palette. Six named roles, so no single value quietly acquires a second meaning. `--no-color`, `--plain` and `--color=<auto|always|never>` are new, and are stripped from argv before dispatch since colour is a property of the terminal rather than of any command.

## USAGE

The 985-character single-line constant is now a grouped listing. `tests/family_lock.rs` asserted on one concatenated fragment; that is now two positive assertions and one negative, which is stricter than what it replaced — it would catch one verb's arguments drifting while the other's did not.

## Cost paid

Test inventory 600 → 616 hub, 819 → 835 total, with both identity digests regenerated by running `ops/ci/test-partitions.sh` rather than by editing numbers. 16 new tests, no skipped or ignored test.

Proved on the development host: the whole `fast` lane green at 616/616, and every new test failing when the behaviour it describes is removed.

title: Publish the dev-node lane at canonical paths and pin its harness as proof-only
body:
Closes the finding `operator_review` raised four times: the dev-node lane could not be found at any canonical path, because it only ever existed in a scratch tree on the development host.

## What lands

| Path | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `devnode/README.md` | Why the lane cannot be hosted, and two things about this console a future test author would otherwise rediscover the hard way |
| `devnode/tui/{Cargo.toml,Cargo.lock,tests/tui.rs}` | Eight TUIWright flows driving the **installed** `bullet` binary through a real pseudo-terminal |
| `ops/ci/devnode.sh` | The lane driver: typed refusals for every missing prerequisite, both Playwright halves mandatory |
| `scripts/ci-local.sh`, `ops/ci/artifact-check.sh`, `scripts/ci-doctor.sh` | Lane registry entries |
| `ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh` + test | The hosted-refusal guard and its hostile fixtures |
| `ops/ci/lib.sh` + `ops/ci/rust-build-subject-test.sh` | Proof-only manifest classification |

## The manifest question, resolved the way the reviewers asked

My first attempt pruned `./devnode` from the build-subject search. Both reviewers rejected it, and they were right — pruning would have made every future manifest under that directory invisible to the guard.

There are now two pinned classes. Product manifests are what ships. Proof manifests belong to harnesses that are never a product dependency and are built by no lane other than the one they prove; `crates/bullet-wire/fuzz/Cargo.toml` set the precedent and `devnode/tui/Cargo.toml` joins it. Both the manifest and its lock are digest-pinned exactly as a product manifest is.

**The four product manifest pins and the seven existing subject pins are byte-identical to main.**

Four new canary cases cover precisely what pruning would have let through:

- a second harness beside the pinned one → `CARGO_MANIFEST_INVENTORY_DRIFT`
- the pinned harness removed → `CARGO_MANIFEST_INVENTORY_DRIFT`
- a changed harness dependency → `RUST_BUILD_SUBJECT_DRIFT`
- a changed harness lock → `RUST_BUILD_SUBJECT_DRIFT`

## Why the lane refuses to be hosted

It drives the real console and the real browser against an authenticated operator session. That session and the provider credentials behind it exist on one machine. A hosted copy could only ever prove something weaker while carrying the name of a lane that claims much more, so it is refused twice: `ops/ci/devnode.sh` refuses under `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, and `ops/ci/workflow-policy.sh` refuses any hosted workflow that names it. The second guard has hostile fixtures for a job that runs the lane, a commented-out mention, a matrix entry, and a symlinked workflow entry.

## Proved locally before pushing

- the full `lint` lane passes end to end
- the build-subject canary passes, and fails with `RUST_BUILD_SUBJECT_DRIFT` when the new pin is falsified
- the workflow policy passes, and fails with `WORKFLOW_DEVNODE_HOSTILE_FAILED` when the devnode guard is neutered
